what: Whether admitting a project's own ground at line scope changes what the model namer implicates — the path that runs in production — across several outcomes, two grounds and several model families. Recall is whether `expect` is reached; the domain count beside it is what reaching it cost.
caveats: One run per cell at temperature 0. G4 is the exception and is the point of it: its ground admits no lines, so its two rows are byte-identical input and their gap is this panel's noise floor.

Every family here is untuned by the repo's own matrix (hosts/tuning.ts names only claude), so all of them ran best-effort. The model behind the run §20 recorded is not written down anywhere in this repo and cannot be placed on this panel.
The keyword arm concatenates the admitted lines; the namer arm labels them as the project's own documents. Compare conditions within an arm; across arms, only the direction is comparable.

A row carrying `namerFailure` is unmeasured: the namer threw and the shipped keyword fallback answered in its place. Read the presence of that field, not inferredBy — a fallback whose keywords also found nothing reports inferredBy "none", which on a clean row means the namer considered the catalog and named nothing.

The outcomes were written for this measurement by an Anthropic model reading each ground; only G1 is verbatim from a recorded run. Items were chosen for whether the ground carries a binding at all, which is what makes an item valid, and never on how a model answered it.
The namer prompt asks for a reason grounded in the outcome's own words, so a `why` that does not quote an admitted line is not evidence the line was ignored.
`why` was added to the probe partway through the panel and is absent on the cells recorded before that; the domains and counts on those cells are unaffected.
